messages:
Ashok: Quick question — enterprise customer on a Private deployment asked for a list of outbound IPs to whitelist. Do we provide static egress CIDRs for Dedicated/Private, or should they point a proxy at us?

Sara: Short answer: Dedicated offers region-scoped static egress allocations we can share. Hosted API uses large ephemeral pools (NOT suitable for strict whitelists). Private (customer-managed VPC / on‑prem) depends on their NAT/proxy — we can't force their outbound IP.

Ashok: Customer wants explicit CIDRs they can paste into their firewall rule. They prefer not to run a proxy.

Ben: Options to give them (pick one):
1) If they want static IPs: opt for Dedicated. We can allocate EGRESS CIDRs for the tenant per region (example doc test CIDRs below).
2) If they keep Private but want stable egress, they need to provision a NAT/GW with Elastic IP(s) on their side (or sit behind a corporate proxy with static egress).
3) For Hosted customers: whitelist domains and/or use a corporate proxy. Hosted public IPs are ephemeral and not recommended for strict allowlist rules.

Ben: Example CIDRs we use in docs (these are doc/test ranges — production allocations will be specific to the tenant and region):
- 198.51.100.0/24 (us-west-2 example pool)
- 203.0.113.0/25 (eu-west-1 example pool)
- 192.0.2.0/28 (small reserved block for control-plane callbacks)

Olga: Proxy requirements to call Redwood endpoints:
- Proxy must support HTTP CONNECT for TLS tunnels (port 443).
- Allow websocket upgrades for streaming responses (if they use streaming).
- Do NOT terminate TLS unless they can add exceptions — TLS MITM breaks client certs and mTLS.
- If using corp TLS inspection, we'll need the customer to add exceptions for our domains or provide pinning guidance.

Ashok: Can you paste exact firewall rules I can send to their infra team?

Ben: Sure — example rules (vendor-agnostic):
```
# allow outbound to Redwood regional egress CIDRs
allow out to 198.51.100.0/24 tcp dport 443
allow out to 203.0.113.0/25 tcp dport 443
# allow DNS to our name servers / resolution
allow out to 192.0.2.53 udp dport 53
# if using proxy on site
allow out to proxy.corp.company tcp dport 3128
```
Proxy-specific checklist:
```
- permit CONNECT to *.redwood-inference.com:443 (SNI allowlist OK)
- permit long-lived TCP connections (>= 5m idle) for streaming
- support HTTP/2 and keepalive for better tail latency
```

infra-bot: NOTE: Dedicated egress allocation updated for tenant d-01 in region us-west-2 — reserved block 198.51.100.16/28. Ticket: DED-ALLOC-128.

Ashok: Great — I'll send these rules along. Any docs I should link?

Sara: Send them this snippet + our KB (internal link): https://redwood-internal.kb/egress-guide (include dedicated vs hosted section). Also warn them about routing/proxy latency: routing through a proxy in a different region can add ~50–150ms RTT. Recommend colocating NAT/proxy in same AZ as workload.

Olga: FYI I opened INC-3457 to track follow-up (cert guidance + dedicated allocation confirmation).

Ashok: Thanks team :thumbsup:
